text:
ConocoPhillips rose 1.6% today to $142.28, continuing a recovery that's gained nearly $6 in the past three trading days. The bounce appears tied to stabilization in oil prices—US crude is holding around $89.62 per barrel—and a shift in market sentiment after weeks of weakness. Recent headlines suggesting potential de-escalation in Middle East tensions (Trump's comments on Iran, the Bessent security move signaling continued US diplomatic focus) may have eased some of the downward pressure that sent the stock down 7.6% over the past two weeks.

The broader context: Russian crude output rebounded to 8.73 million barrels per day in October, and the IEA noted global oil markets have shifted into surplus. That surplus typically pressures prices, which had been a headwind for the stock. Today's move reflects traders betting that geopolitical risk premiums—baked into oil prices during periods of Iran tensions—could persist or stabilize, even if the fundamental supply-demand picture remains soft.
